QuestionStmt.S: Calculate $\Delta S_{\text{total}}$ for a certain reaction at 298 K if $\Delta H^\circ = -208.6 \, \text{kJ}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = -36 \, \text{J K}^{-1}$

Solution.S:
Given:
$$\Delta H^\circ = -208.6 \, \text{kJ}$$
$$\Delta S^\circ = -36 \, \text{J K}^{-1}$$
$$T = 298 \, \text{K}$$

First, convert $\Delta H^\circ$ from kJ to J:
$$\Delta H^\circ = -208.6 \, \text{kJ} = -208600 \, \text{J}$$

Step 1: Calculate the entropy change of the surroundings ($\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$):

By NCERT method,
$$\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -\frac{\Delta H^\circ}{T}$$

Substitute the values:
$$\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -\frac{-208600 \, \text{J}}{298 \, \text{K}} = \frac{208600 \, \text{J}}{298 \, \text{K}} \, \text{J K}^{-1}$$

Calculate:
$$\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} \approx 700 \, \text{J K}^{-1}$$

Step 2: Calculate the total entropy change ($\Delta S_{\text{total}}$):

$$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{system}} + \Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$$

Substitute the values:
$$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = -36 \, \text{J K}^{-1} + 700 \, \text{J K}^{-1} = 664 \, \text{J K}^{-1}$$

Final Answer: Option A: $664 \, \text{J K}^{-1}$
